evidence.title: North Sentinel Island (Andaman Archipelago): Sentinelese coastal lifeways
evidence.dateBasis: Indirect comparative baseline: Andamanese Onge/Jarawa genetics and colonial/modern historical logs (1771, 1867 Nineveh, 1880 Portman abduction); zero direct archaeological or genetic sampling on North Sentinel.
evidence.summary: Home to the Sentinelese, who maintain an unclassified language, shallow outrigger-canoe reef fishing, forest pig hunting, and cold-forged shipwreck iron tools while repulsing external contact since colonial trauma in 1880. See Deep Dive for post-1900 PATR exclusion, 2004 M9.1–9.3 coral reef uplift, and 2018 events.
evidence.limits: Timeline ends at 1900 CE per atlas convention; zero excavated stratigraphy or direct DNA exists for North Sentinel Island itself.

evidence.title: Fashoda / Kodok: Shilluk (Chollo) Reth Sacred Monarchy (South Sudan)
evidence.dateBasis: Nilotic oral dynastic traditions (c. 1500 CE Reth Nyikang consolidation), mound settlement archaeology along the White Nile, and 19th-century historical documentation.
evidence.summary: Sacred royal capital of the Shilluk Reth dynasty controlling rich seasonal floodplains along the upper White Nile north of the Sudd marshes, uniting Nilotic sorghum farming, cattle keeping, and river canoe trade.
evidence.limits: Upper White Nile swampy alluvial plains obscure deep mound stratigraphy prior to 1500 CE.

evidence.title: Lokanaya & Bahr el-Ghazal Pastoral Mound Settlements (South Sudan)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates on seasonal wetland habitation mounds spanning Nilotic cattle pastoralism, fishing, and early sorghum cultivation along Bahr el-Ghazal tributaries.
evidence.summary: Constructed artificial dry-island earthen mounds enabling year-round flood-season cattle herds, sorghum gardens, and early iron bloomery metallurgy across South Sudan's seasonal Sudd wetlands.
evidence.limits: Sparse systematic excavation across South Sudan leaves regional Iron Age transitions coarsely bracketed.

evidence.title: Kullaty & Dyuktai Middle Lena Valley Sequence (Yakutia, Central Siberia)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Lena terrace permafrost sequences linking Dyuktai microblades with Sumnagin, Belkachi, and Ymyiakhtakh Neolithic-Bronze complexes.
evidence.summary: Continuous subarctic Lena Valley hunting, net fishing, and cord-impressed Neolithic ceramic camps connecting Beringian microblade foragers with Yakut-area metallurgy thresholds.
evidence.limits: Permafrost cryoturbation mixes thin cultural lenses across flooded Lena terraces.

evidence.title: Arzhan-2 Royal Scythian Kurgan (Uyuk Valley, Tuva)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology on larch chamber logs (~640–620 BCE) and intact gold-mounted Steppe-Scythian grave goods.
evidence.summary: Unlooted 7th-century BCE royal stone mound yielding ~20 kg of animal-style gold jewelry, silk traces, lacquerware, and sacrificial riding horses—the richest early Aldy-Bel steppe tomb in Inner Asia.
evidence.limits: Monumental elite burial reflects royal networks rather than common steppe campsites.

evidence.title: Osipovka Late Glacial Early Pottery Complex (Lower Amur, Khabarovsk)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on charred food crusts, plant fiber tempers, and lipid residues (~14,000–11,000 cal BP).
evidence.summary: Among the world's oldest ceramic vessels—thick fiber-tempered pots used by semi-sedentary Lower Amur hunter-fisher camps to render seasonal anadromous salmon oils during the Pleistocene–Holocene transition.
evidence.limits: Acidic Amur river gravels preserve pottery sherds better than unburned bone.

evidence.title: Ushki Lake Stratified Paleolithic-to-Holocene Camps (Kamchatka)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon from stratified volcanic tephra-sealed Layer VII (stemmed bifaces) and Layer VI dwellings beside Kamchatka River.
evidence.summary: Key Beringian-Pacific gateway campsite preserving subterranean dwellings, ochre-sprinkled child/dog burials, stemmed projectile points, and salmon-spawning lake camps.
evidence.limits: Re-dating in the 2000s revised initial ~14 ka estimates younger to ~11,000–10,600 cal BCE.

evidence.title: Chertovy Vorota Neolithic Woven-Fiber Cave (Primorye)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon on charred wooden roof-beams, woven sedge textiles, and 7,700-year-old ancient human genomes.
evidence.summary: Burned Neolithic log-and-wattle cave dwelling preserving twisted cord nets, woven mats, antler harpoons, and genomes demonstrating deep maternal-and-autosomal continuity to modern Lower Amur Ulchi speakers.
evidence.limits: Single catastrophic roof-fire episode freezes one Neolithic household generation.

evidence.title: Murujuga (Burrup Peninsula) & Dampier Petroglyphs (Pilbara, WA)
evidence.dateBasis: Weathering sequences on gabbro rock-varnish depictions of extinct thylacines paired with >9,000-year coastal middens and historical contact accounts.
evidence.summary: Over one million pecked gabbro engravings across Yapurarra Country tracking the dramatic post-glacial shift from inland arid kangaroo-and-thylacine hunting to coastal mangrove & marine turtle foraging.
evidence.limits: Direct mineral-varnish absolute dating remains technically difficult for bare rock engravings.

evidence.title: Puntutjarpa Rockshelter (Western Desert, Western Australia)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified hearth radiocarbon dates and classic desert adze-flake sequences excavated with Ngaanyatjarra Elders.
evidence.summary: Benchmark Western Desert occupation shelter documenting uninterrupted adaptive survival through mid-Holocene hyper-aridity using hafted tula adzes, seed grinding slabs, and tiny ephemeral water-soak mobility.
evidence.limits: Dry desert deflation outside rock overhangs removes open-air camp stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Xinglongwa & Chahai Early Millet Villages (Liaoxi, Inner Mongolia–Liaoning)
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dating on carbonized broomcorn millet (Panicum miliaceum) and enclosed sunken house pits.
evidence.summary: Ditch-enclosed planned villages containing Asia's earliest nephrite jade earrings, dragon-mosaic pebble sculptures (Chahai), and domesticated broomcorn millet agriculture across Manchuria.
evidence.limits: Early farming supplemented heavily by broad-spectrum acorn, walnut, and wild pig foraging.

evidence.title: Wandu / Guonei Koguryo Royal Tombs & Capitals (Ji'an, Jilin)
evidence.dateBasis: Monumental 414 CE Stele of King Gwanggaeto and ~7,000 stepped-stone Koguryo royal tombs.
evidence.summary: Mountain-fortress and Yalu river-plain dual capital complex of the northern Koguryo Kingdom blending Chinese administrative architecture with Northeast Asian painted astronomical tomb chambers.
evidence.limits: Capital moved south to Pyongyang in 427 CE, though royal tombs continued in use.

evidence.title: Shangjing Longquanfu (Bohai / Balhae Kingdom Capital, Heilongjiang)
evidence.dateBasis: Rammed-earth Tang-plan city walls, imperial palace roof tiles, and Liao conquest chronicles (926 CE).
evidence.summary: Supreme northern capital of the Mohe–Koguryo multi-ethnic Bohai state (~16 km circuit patterned after Chang'an), featuring volcanic basalt garden pavilions and Furong ceramics traded across the Sea of Japan.
evidence.limits: Built over earlier Mohe towns and burned during the 926 CE Khitan-Liao conquest.

evidence.title: Tanum Bronze Age Rock Carvings & Longboat Galleries (Bohuslän, Sweden)
evidence.dateBasis: Shoreline uplift elevation curves along Skagerrak granite ridges matched to Bronze Age ship prows and lur horns.
evidence.summary: Over 600 pecked coastal granite panels depicting hundreds of high-prowed Nordic Bronze Age oared ships, sun-wheel chariots, plows, and bronze lures along an emerging archipelago.
evidence.limits: Post-glacial isostatic rebound dates shoreline panels broadly across Bronze Age phases.

evidence.title: Gamla Uppsala Royal Mounds & Mälaren Trade Axis (Sweden)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates of Great Mounds (~550–625 CE), Vendel–Viking boat graves, and Christian archbishopric transfer.
evidence.summary: Paramount religious-and-royal center of Iron-to-Viking-Age eastern Sweden, anchored by three monumental 6th-century earth mounds, monumental hall terraces, and silver/furs moving to Birka and Sigtuna.
evidence.limits: Pre-Christian temple forms described by Adam of Bremen remain debated against excavated posthole halls.

evidence.title: Kunda Lammasmägi & Pulli Mesolithic Settlements (Estonia)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon on elk-bone harpoons, black flint cores, and post-Ancylus Lake shorelines.
evidence.summary: Eponymous Eastern Baltic Mesolithic pioneer horizon showing specialized elk/seal bone-point craftsmanship, amber ornament use, and rapid post-glacial recolonization along emerging Baltic lagoons.
evidence.limits: Kunda Hill gravel mining disturbed part of the eastern shoreline occupation.

evidence.title: Yengema & Kamabai Forest Rock Shelters (Sierra Leone)
evidence.dateBasis: Thermoluminescence and radiocarbon sequence bracketing polished dolerite celts, impressed pottery, and Iron Age transition.
evidence.summary: Crucial Upper Guinea forest-savanna transition shelters preserving early stone celts ('nomoli' tradition landscape), earliest ironworking ~7th–8th century CE, and steatite carving ancestors.
evidence.limits: Acidic West African rainforest soils dissolve skeletal remains and plant macroremains.

evidence.title: Kong Dyula Mosque & Savanna Caravan City (Northern Côte d'Ivoire)
evidence.dateBasis: Sudano-Sahelian adobe Great Mosque traditions, Mande-Dyula manuscript networks, and 18th-century Kong Emirate records.
evidence.summary: Premier Mande Dyula Islamic scholarship and kola-cloth-gold caravan crossroads linking Forest-belt Akan goldfields north to Jenné and Timbuktu before Samori Touré's 1897 devastation.
evidence.limits: Urban adobe mosque rebuildings and 1897 destruction leave deep urban medieval layers lightly probed.

evidence.title: Arkaim & Sintashta Fortified Chariot Citadel (Southern Trans-Urals)
evidence.dateBasis: High-precision radiocarbon dates on spoked-wheel chariot burials, horse cheekpieces, and copper-slags (~2050–1800 cal BCE).
evidence.summary: Concentric ring-walled bronze metallurgy fortress where the earliest true two-wheeled horse-drawn spoked chariots appear alongside arsenical-bronze weaponry later linked to steppe Indo-Iranian dispersals.
evidence.limits: Exact sociopolitical scale debated between egalitarian pastoralist chiefdoms and fortified clan hubs.

evidence.title: Chicha-1 Proto-Urban Baraba Forest-Steppe Settlement (West Siberia)
evidence.dateBasis: Magnetometry plan of >100 semi-subterranean houses and AMS radiocarbon across Irmen–Krasnoozerka horizons.
evidence.summary: Planned ~24-hectare fortified Late Bronze/Early Iron transition proto-town between Ob and Irtysh showing dense permanent bronze workshops and long-distance steppe-taiga fur exchange.
evidence.limits: Geophysical surveys dominate; only selected citadel sectors were excavated in detail.

evidence.title: Shigir Peat Bog Carved Larch Idol (Middle Urals)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dating by Zhilin et al. (2018) on newly felled heartwood of the 5.3 m carved Larix trunk.
evidence.summary: World's oldest monumental wooden sculpture: a 5.3-meter Preboreal larch post incised with eight geometric-and-human faces using polished beaver-incisor chisels millennia before Ural farming.
evidence.limits: Exhumed by gold prospectors in 1890 without stratigraphic context; dated directly on inner wood.

evidence.title: Lake Onega & White Sea Karelia Petroglyphs (NW Russia)
evidence.dateBasis: Shoreline uplift elevation dating and associated Pit-Comb Ware coastal settlements.
evidence.summary: Over 4,500 quartz-and-granite engravings—swan-headed solar motifs, whaling skiffs, and ski hunters—depicting Mesolithic-to-Neolithic boreal spirituality across Fennoscandian shores.
evidence.limits: Granite bedrock panels lack organic pigment binders for direct radiocarbon measurement.

evidence.title: Begazy-Dandybai Elite Stone Mausolea (Central Kazakh Steppe)
evidence.dateBasis: Ashlar granite megalithic burial enclosures and Karasuk-linked bronze daggers/tin-mining crucibles.
evidence.summary: Monumental Final Bronze Age terraced granite mausolea built near rich copper and tin mining belts of Ulytau and Kent, marking centralized steppe metallurgy prior to mobile Scythian nomadism.
evidence.limits: Many elite stone chambers suffered ancient looting; domestic Kent town excavations clarify settlement hierarchy.

evidence.title: Tamgaly Gorge Bronze Age Petroglyph Sanctuary (Semirechye, Kazakhstan)
evidence.dateBasis: Stylistic-chisel sequence linking Andronovo sun-headed deities to Saka-Wusun horsemen and Old Turkic runiform inscriptions.
evidence.summary: Iconic steppe ritual gorge bearing ~5,000 Bronze-to-Turkic canyon carvings—crowned sun-headed figures, twin horses, ritual dances—set beside ancestral kist burials.
evidence.limits: Overlaying multiple periods across single sandstone faces complicates sub-phase boundary precision.

evidence.title: Daojali Hading & Naga–Khasi Megalithic Highlands (NE India)
evidence.dateBasis: Cord-marked pottery and shouldered celts (Daojali Hading) paired with living Austroasiatic/Tibeto-Burman menhir lineages.
evidence.summary: Archaeological corridor connecting East/SE Asia and South Asia: ground shouldered jadeite celts, double-shouldered hoes, cord-marked ceramics, and living megalithic commemoration stones across Assam, Nagaland, and Meghalaya.
evidence.limits: Early Northeast Indian Neolithic sites lack high-precision AMS programs compared to mainland SE Asia.

evidence.title: Halin & Beikthano Early Pyu Brick-Walled Cities (Upper Myanmar)
evidence.dateBasis: Thermoluminescence on kiln-fired curved bricks, Brahmi Pyu inscriptions, and radiating canal-irrigation dams.
evidence.summary: Earliest urbanized hydraulic settlements in mainland SE Asia predating Bagan—monumental finger-marked brick fortifications, silver rising-sun coinage, and cremation urn cemeteries linked to Indian Buddhist networks.
evidence.limits: Continuous brick reuse in medieval dynasties obscure pre-2nd-century CE foundations.

evidence.title: Shizhaishan Royal Necropolis of the Dian Kingdom (Lake Dian, Yunnan)
evidence.dateBasis: Han Emperor Wu's golden 'Seal of the King of Dian' (109 BCE) paired with vivid cast lost-wax bronze drum-cowrie scenes.
evidence.summary: Dramatic Southwest Silk Road culture renowned for intricate lost-wax bronze cowrie containers filled with coastal Indian Ocean shells and depicting multi-ethnic agricultural rites, warfare, and sacrificial bull altars.
evidence.limits: Waterlogged burial acidity destroyed most non-bronze organics except gilt cowrie caches.

evidence.title: Wairau Bar Early Polynesian Village (Marlborough, Aotearoa/NZ)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS dates on moa eggshell and charcoal + ancient mtDNA/isotopes + Tropical East Polynesian pearl-shell lure & Terebra chisels.
evidence.summary: Flagship first-generation Māori ancestral landing and moa-hunting village beside a coastal gravel spit—yielding East Polynesian argillite adzes, moa-egg water flasks, reef-shell lures, and early Aotearoa settlement life.
evidence.limits: Intrusive mid-20th-century gravel extraction and reburial agreements constrain re-excavation.

evidence.title: Bourewa & Sigatoka Sand Dunes Lapita Sequence (Viti Levu, Fiji)
evidence.dateBasis: Basal Lapita dentate-stamped earthenware radiocarbon (~1050 cal BCE) & Sigatoka dune burial chronology.
evidence.summary: Earliest Lapita founding settlements in Fiji marking the critical easternmost launchpad of Remote Oceanic outrigger voyaging (~1050 BCE), preserving thousands of obsidian-tempered sherds and coastal fish-and-turtle middens.
evidence.limits: Mobile coastal sand dunes episodically erode and rebury occupational horizons.

evidence.title: Laura / Quinkan Sandstone Rock Art & Early Mushroom Rock (Cape York)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Mushroom Rock / Early Man Shelter dates (>15,000–40,000 BP ground ochre crayons) and Quinkan sandstone galleries.
evidence.summary: Monumental red-and-white Quinkan spirit paintings, boomerang stencils, and excavated sandstone rockshelters recording uninterrupted Cape York Aboriginal ceremonial art and stone-tool continuity from Pleistocene groundstone use to colonial frontier survival.
evidence.limits: Direct radiocarbon dating of non-beeswax mineral iron-oxide pigment layers remains rare.

evidence.title: Kenniff Cave Pleistocene–Holocene Sequence (Carnarvon Gorge, Queensland)
evidence.dateBasis: Landmark 1960–1964 Mulvaney excavation producing the first radiocarbon proof (>16,000 BP) of Pleistocene humanity in Australia.
evidence.summary: Historic Carnarvon Range sandstone shelter whose deep ash layers demonstrated >20,000 years of Australian Aboriginal antiquity, crowned with negative-stencil hand galleries and backed-blade shifts.
evidence.limits: Classic 1960s conventional charcoal ages underestimate earliest basal sands compared to modern OSL.

evidence.title: Burrill Lake & Sydney Basin Sandstone Shelters (NSW)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates (~20,800 BP basal occupation at Burrill Lake) tracked alongside mid-Holocene coastal estuarine shell middens.
evidence.summary: Key eastern Australian rockshelter documenting inland ice-age plateau camp origins before post-glacial sea-level rise drowned the shelf and turned Burrill into a rich Yuin estuarine fishery.
evidence.limits: Glacial-maximum coastal plains now lie submerged offshore on the continental shelf.

evidence.title: Imbonga & Equatorial Tshuapa Rainforest Pottery Horizon (DRC)
evidence.dateBasis: River-survey charcoal radiocarbon (~400–100 BCE) anchored to distinctive flat-based grooved Imbonga vessels.
evidence.summary: Pioneer equatorial rainforest river settlements along the Ruki–Momboyo–Tshuapa confluence showing rapid Bantu-speaking riverine colonization combining oil-palm harvesting, plantain phytolith proxies, and ceramic innovation.
evidence.limits: Thick equatorial canopy obscures non-riverine upland settlement sites.

evidence.title: Kamilamba & Kabambian Copper-Cross Metallurgy (Upper Congo–Lomami)
evidence.dateBasis: Chronometric grave-series transition from standardized H-shaped Katanga copper croisettes to micro-ingot currency bars.
evidence.summary: Monetization and political centralization of the Luba coreland documented through standardized cast copper croisette ingots, iron ceremonial axes, and glass trade beads linking central savanna lakes to Indian/Atlantic merchants.
evidence.limits: Cemetery bias stresses prestige metallurgy over everyday rural manioc/millet homesteads.

evidence.title: Opone / Ras Hafun Indian Ocean Emporium (Puntland, Somalia)
evidence.dateBasis: Roman red-gloss, Mesopotamian Parthian-Sasanian blue-glazed wares, and Nile amphorae described in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.
evidence.summary: Excavated peninsula port at Cape Guardafui corner matching the Periplus' Opone—exporting cinnamon-transit cargoes, tortoise shell, and aromatics between Egypt, Arabia, Persia, and monsoon India.
evidence.limits: Short 1976 coastal trenching remains unrepeated since due to regional security constraints.

evidence.title: Mogadishu (Hamar Weyne) & Barawa Benadir Coral-Stone Sultanates
evidence.dateBasis: Dated 1269 CE Fakhr al-Din Mosque and 1238 CE Arba'a Rukun Kufic inscriptions + Ibn Battuta's 1331 CE eye-witness account.
evidence.summary: Prosperous Somali Benadir coast coral-rag port confederations weaving patterned Benadir cotton textiles ('al-maqdashi') and minting Sultanate coinage linking Abyssinian highlands to Kilwa, Aden, and Gujarat.
evidence.limits: Modern urban overburden limits sub-12th-century stratigraphic trenches beneath Old Hamar.

evidence.title: Karuo High-Altitude Millet Village (Chamdo, Eastern Tibet)
evidence.dateBasis: Carbonized foxtail & broomcorn millet AMS dates at 3,100 m elevation in Upper Mekong terrace soils.
evidence.summary: Key eastern Himalayan agricultural gateway demonstrating cold-tolerant foxtail millet expansion onto the 3,100-meter Tibetan Plateau alongside double-room stone houses and painted Majiayao-linked pottery.
evidence.limits: Lower-altitude seasonal valley village preceding year-round >3,500 m barley permanent settlement.

evidence.title: Lumbini Ashokan Timber-Brick Shrine & Mustang Sky Caves (Nepal)
evidence.dateBasis: 2013 OSL & 14C dating of pre-Ashokan ~550 BCE timber postholes under the Maya Devi Temple paired with ~249 BCE Ashoka pillar.
evidence.summary: World's oldest dated Buddhist sanctuary foundation (~6th c. BCE timber railing around a central tree-shrine) spanning the Terai plain up to Upper Mustang's painted cliff-cave monasteries in trans-Himalayan Nepal.
evidence.limits: Dating of exact Siddhartha Gautama birth decade within the 6th–5th c. BCE bracket remains scholarly debate.

evidence.title: Lhasa Jokhang, Samye & Yarlung Royal Capitals (Central Tibet)
evidence.dateBasis: Jokhang architectural timber dates (mid-7th c. Songtsen Gampo) and 821–823 CE bilingual Sino-Tibetan treaty stele.
evidence.summary: Imperial and religious heartland of the Pugyal Tibetan Empire (Yarlung tomb mounds, Lhasa Jokhang 639 CE, Samye 779 CE, and Potala Palace 1645 CE) linking Tang, Silk Road, Nepalese, and Indian traditions.
evidence.limits: High plateau urban continuity repeatedly restored temples over early imperial stonework.

evidence.title: Sungai Batu & Bujang Valley Iron-Smelting Entrepôt (Kedah, Malaysia)
evidence.dateBasis: OSL & radiocarbon assays of Tuyere iron-smelting furnaces and river-jetty bricks along ancient Muda estuary.
evidence.summary: Major Southeast Asian port and industrialized iron-smelting center (producing bloomery steel ingots alongside earliest SE Asian brick stupa foundations) supplying trans-peninsular Malacca Strait maritime shipping.
evidence.limits: Reworked coastal river silts; ongoing peer review refines earliest 5th–6th c. BCE OSL foundry dates.

evidence.title: Muaro Jambi Brick Buddhist Temple Complex (Batang Hari, Sumatra)
evidence.dateBasis: Palawa-to-Old-Malay inscribed gold plates, brick candi canal-moats, and Chinese Tang-Yuan trade sherds.
evidence.summary: Southeast Asia's largest brick Buddhist university-entrepôt complex (>2,600 ha along the Batang Hari River) associated with Malayu–Srivijaya monastic scholarship visited by Atīśa and Chinese pilgrims.
evidence.limits: Brick superstructures heavily overgrown prior to 1970s–2020s restoration.

evidence.title: Kutai Mulawarman Sanskrit Yūpa Inscriptions (East Kalimantan, Borneo)
evidence.dateBasis: Paleographic dating of seven Pallava-Grantha Sanskrit sacrificial post inscriptions from Muara Kaman.
evidence.summary: Earliest written historical inscriptions in the Indonesian Archipelago, recording King Mulawarman's Vedic cattle-and-gold donations along the Mahakam River at the eastern edge of Austronesian Borneo.
evidence.limits: Found clustered out of original temple context near Muara Kaman.

evidence.title: Lothal Harappan Tidal Dockyard & Carnelian Workshop (Gujarat)
evidence.dateBasis: Mature Harappan radiocarbon series, baked-brick 219×37 m basin, and stamped Dilmun/Persian Gulf seals.
evidence.summary: Southernmost planned Harappan port town featuring a monumental baked-brick wharf/dock basin linked by palaeochannels to the Gulf of Khambhat, carnelian etched-bead workshops, ivory scales, and Gulf cretulae seals.
evidence.limits: Debated whether the large brick tank served solely as tidal boat dock or freshwater/industrial reservoir.

evidence.title: Kalibangan Harappan Citadel & Ploughed Field (Ghaggar Basin, Rajasthan)
evidence.dateBasis: Early-to-Mature Harappan radiocarbon sequence, preserved dual-furrow ploughed field (c. 2800 BCE), and mudbrick fire-altars.
evidence.summary: Earliest archaeologically preserved ploughed agricultural field in South Asia (cross-grid furrows for mustard and chickpea) sealed below a planned Mature Harappan mudbrick citadel and lower town.
evidence.limits: Pre-AMS 1960s dates yield wide sigma errors; re-dating confirms early third-millennium start.

evidence.title: Trowulan Hydraulic Capital of the Majapahit Empire (East Java)
evidence.dateBasis: 14th-century Nagarakretagama panegyric matched to satellite-mapped 11×9 km brick canal grid, Segaran reservoir, and Ming porcelains.
evidence.summary: Capital of maritime SE Asia's largest pre-colonial archipelagic thalassocracy, uniting monumental red-brick Hindu-Buddhist gateways (Wringin Lawang), hydraulic fishponds, terracotta workshops, and spice tributes.
evidence.limits: Modern agricultural settlements overlie much of the former bamboo-and-timber royal quarters.

evidence.title: Sembiran Indian-Trade Port & Subak Irrigated Rice System (Bali)
evidence.dateBasis: Rouletted Ware / Arikamedu sherds & Old Balinese copper plates (896 CE Pura Ulun Danu Batur) documenting Subak water-temples.
evidence.summary: Dual anchor showing Bali's early 1st-century BCE Rouletted Ware maritime contact with South India and East Java (Sembiran) alongside its enduring democratic water-temple terraced rice engineering (Subak, epigraphically attested from 9th c. CE).
evidence.limits: Deep Sembiran volcanic beach trenches yield sherds across reworked coastal wave-cut strata.

evidence.title: Lore Lindu (Bada, Besoa & Napu) Megalithic Statues (Central Sulawesi)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified kalamba urn-and-burial radiocarbon spans associated with >400 carved andesite anthropomorphic statues.
evidence.summary: Highland valley megalithic phenomenon featuring 1.5–4.5 m cylindrical stone statues ('arca'), massive lidded kalamba stone burial vats, and stone mortar basins in mountainous Central Sulawesi.
evidence.limits: Carved standing granite/andesite monoliths are mostly isolated on open grass plateaus lacking stratigraphic seals.

evidence.title: Karkar–Aitape & Massim Kula Obsidian-Shell Seascape (Coastal New Guinea)
evidence.dateBasis: Talasea-origin volcanic obsidian hydration & XRF provenancing combined with Milne Bay/Massim pottery exchange chronologies.
evidence.summary: Long-distance canoe networks binding northern New Guinea islands, Lapita potters, and the Trobriand-Massim Kula ring—exchanging white Conus armlets, red Spondylus necklaces, sago, and Bismarck obsidian blades.
evidence.limits: Chronological transition from prehistoric obsidian circuits to the ethnographic Kula ring remains coarse.

evidence.title: Biskupin Lusatian Timber-Walled Lake Fortress (Poland)
evidence.dateBasis: Annual tree-ring dendrochronology of waterlogged oak ramparts (winter 748/747 BCE–722 BCE).
evidence.summary: Remarkably preserved Hallstatt/Lusatian 106-house planned island timber fortress ringed by wave-breakers and pine corduroy streets in Greater Poland—reconstructed to the exact year via dendrochronology.
evidence.limits: Water-table drainage partially compressed organic upper turf roofs prior to museum preservation.

evidence.title: Sarmizegetusa Regia Dacian Mountain Citadel & Andesite Sanctuaries (Romania)
evidence.dateBasis: Decebalus-era iron workshops, Latin-stamped legionary demolition (Trajan 106 CE), and circular andesite calendar sanctuary.
evidence.summary: Monumental 1,200-meter Carpathian political and religious capital of pre-Roman Dacia—combining Hellenistic murus dacicus stone fortifications, terraced iron forges, and aligned circular andesite column sanctuaries.
evidence.limits: Astronomical orientations of the Great Circular Sanctuary remain actively debated against Roman-era destruction.

evidence.title: Iwelen & Azelik Copper-Iron Metallurgy (Aïr Mountains, Niger)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon on chariot-period Aïr graves and Azelik (Takedda) native copper smelting furnaces.
evidence.summary: Southern Saharan copper-and-iron innovation node featuring engraved Libyco-Berber chariot-horsemen panels (Iwelen), early copper-working traditions, and later salt-and-copper trade town Takedda visited by Ibn Battuta.
evidence.limits: Low-organic arid gravel contexts complicate fine sub-phase dating of early native copper versus ironworking.

evidence.title: Tibesti Volcanic Highlands: Gonoa & Bardaï Rock Galleries (Northern Chad)
evidence.dateBasis: Basalt canyon engraving superpositions ('Gonoa Man' bubalus-period to camel-cavalry Tebu oases) paired with lacustrine terraces.
evidence.summary: Highland Saharan refugium rising >3,400 m above hyperarid deserts, preserving continuous Holocene engravings from extinct large wild game to Teda/Daza camel-caravan oasis palm agriculture.
evidence.limits: Desert varnish surfaces lack reliable absolute dates outside paleolake shell beds.

evidence.title: Daimabad & Inamgaon Deccan Chalcolithic Farming Towns (Maharashtra)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Savalda, Late Harappan (Daimabad bronzes), Malwa, and Jorwe radiocarbon sequences.
evidence.summary: Largest Deccan Chalcolithic agrarian centers along the Pravara–Ghod rivers featuring irrigation diversion embankments, storage silos, mud-wall compounds, and Daimabad's celebrated solid-cast chariot/elephant-rhino-buffalo bronzes.
evidence.limits: Exact archaeological stratum provenance of the accidentally discovered Daimabad bronze hoard remains debated.

evidence.title: Warangal Kakatiya Citadel & Ramappa Floating-Brick Temple (Telangana)
evidence.dateBasis: Dated Kakatiya Telugu-Sanskrit tank/temple inscriptions (Rudramadevi, Ganapatideva) and Delhi Sultanate siege of 1323 CE.
evidence.summary: Heartland of an eastern Deccan hydraulic empire uniting interconnected cascading tank reservoirs ('Chain of Tanks'), monumental fourfold stone torana gateways at Warangal Fort, and sandbox-foundation lightweight floating-brick sculpture at Ramappa.
evidence.limits: Central Swayambhu shrine destroyed in 1323 CE; surviving toranas mark outer citadel core.

evidence.title: Nanyue King Mausoleum & Qin-Han Panyu Dockyard (Guangzhou, Lingnan)
evidence.dateBasis: Gold seal of Zhao Mo ('Wen Di') inside Xianggang tomb (died c. 122 BCE) paired with Qin-Han wooden shipbuilding slipways.
evidence.summary: Remarkably preserved multi-chamber stone tomb and Han-era shipyard revealing Panyu (Guangzhou) as China's earliest major maritime window to the South China Sea—yielding Persian silver boxes, African elephant tusks, frankincense, and jade burial suits.
evidence.limits: Sinocentric Han conquest histories obscure pre-Qin indigenous Baiyue chiefdom diversity.

evidence.title: Beinan & Dabenkeng Neolithic Jade Villages (Taiwan)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS dating of early Dabenkeng cord-marked millet/rice settlements and >1,500 slate-coffins yielding Hualien Fengtian nephrite jade.
evidence.summary: Crucial Austronesian homeland threshold: Dabenkeng cord-marked coastal villagers crossed the Taiwan Strait before Beinan's monumental slate-slab towns exported green Fengtian nephrite earrings across the Philippines, Vietnam, and Sarawak.
evidence.limits: Coastal paddy farming disturbed upper Iron Age layers; linguistic homeland reconstruction pairs archaeology with Austronesian phylogenies.

evidence.title: Brandberg (Dâures) & White Lady Rock Art Massif (Namibia)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon from Maack and Amis Gorge shelter middens calibrated beneath >43,000 painted granite figures.
evidence.summary: Towering desert granite massif preserving ~900 painted shelters ('White Lady' shamanic procession, eland-and-rain rituals) recording millennia of San hunter-gatherer and later Damara/Nama pastoralist sacred art.
evidence.limits: Most mineral ochre paintings themselves cannot be directly radiocarbon dated.

evidence.title: Benfica & Benguela Early Coastal Shell-and-Iron Settlements (Angola)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon (~2nd century CE Benfica middens south of Luanda) yielding stamped ceramics, marine cowrie-shell currency quarries (nzimbu on Ilha de Luanda), and copper-iron gear.
evidence.summary: Earliest dated Western Bantu coastal Iron Age settlements along northern Angola, supplying marine nzimbu shell currency inland before Kongo and Ndongo state formation.
evidence.limits: Sparse Angolan post-1975 field surveys leave large central plateau belts under-sampled.

evidence.title: Yoshinogari Yayoi Moated Settlement & Watchtowers (Saga, Kyushu)
evidence.dateBasis: Wetted paddy-rice canal stratigraphy, >2,000 ceramic jar-coffins with bronze daggers/silk/glass, and Roman/Han mirror parallels.
evidence.summary: Flagship double-moated and palisaded Yayoi agrarian town (~40 hectares) charting irrigated rice adoption, metallurgy, social warfare (headless skeletons in jar burials), and continental Korean-Chinese bronze ritual imports.
evidence.limits: Chronological debate continues over absolute onset (10th vs. 5th c. BCE) of Northern Kyushu wet-rice paddies.

evidence.title: Shuri Castle & Gusuku Limestone Fortresses of Ryukyu (Okinawa)
evidence.dateBasis: Gusuku coral-limestone ramparts packed with Ming/Yuan celadon tribute wares, Shuri palace foundation stones, and 1879 Meji annexation.
evidence.summary: Independent Ryukyu Kingdom maritime crossroads bridging Ming China, Joseon Korea, Japan, and Malacca–Ayutthaya via monumental stone Gusuku citadel ports and sacred Utaki groves.
evidence.limits: Shuri palace wood superstructures suffered wartime 1945 destruction and 2019 fire, though archaeological foundations remain.

evidence.title: Moyoro Shell Mound & Okhotsk Maritime Culture (Abashiri, Hokkaido)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon, whale-bone toggling harpoons, Amur/Kamchatka mtDNA signatures, and bear-skull altars in hexagonal pit houses.
evidence.summary: Subarctic marine sea-mammal-and-whale hunting society uniting Sakhalin, Kurils, and NE Hokkaido—whose later fusion with Satsumon agriculture formed ancestral Ainu culture.
evidence.limits: Permafrost-free coastal storm erosion threatens outer shell midden rims.

evidence.title: Mahilaka Walled Chlorite-Schist Port & Nosy Mangabe (NW Madagascar)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon + green/blue Islamic sgraffiato and Song-Ming celadon ceramics within 60-hectare coral-walled enclosure.
evidence.summary: Madagascar's largest medieval Swahili–Austronesian–Islamic urbanized port town, exporting turned chloriteschist cooking vessels, rock crystal, gold, and timber across East Africa and the Persian Gulf.
evidence.limits: Floodplain paddy clearance damaged shallow perimeter walls.

evidence.title: Mandrare & Androy Southern Stone Enclosures (South Madagascar)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon on Tandroy Tranovato dry-stone cattle-and-ancestral enclosures and Aepyornis (elephant bird) eggshell middens.
evidence.summary: Semi-arid southern Malagasy pastoralist settlements illustrating the extinction threshold of giant megafauna (Aepyornis, subfossil lemurs) alongside monumental stone-walled Zebu kingdoms.
evidence.limits: Dry spiny-forest surface scatters remain lightly excavated outside Tranovato.

evidence.title: Chersonesus Taurica Greek-to-Byzantine Polis (Sevastopol, Crimea)
evidence.dateBasis: Civic Heraclean Dorian oath stele (c. 300 BCE), orthogonal farm-division 'chora' boundary walls, Roman garrison inscriptions, and Byzantine basilicas.
evidence.summary: Enduring 1,800-year Black Sea port linking Mediterranean wine amphora exports, Scythian grain markets, Roman Crimea fleets, and 988 CE Prince Volodymyr's baptism into Kyivan Rus'.
evidence.limits: Protected Heracleian stone farm grids preserve ancient allotments better than submerged lower harbor quays.

evidence.title: Dereivka Sredny Stog Steppe Settlement (Dnieper, Ukraine)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dating refining Sredny Stog eneolithic layers paired with Dnieper-steppe horse-bone and early steppe ancestry genomes.
evidence.summary: Landmark Eneolithic Dnieper-river camp showcasing mixed Trypillian-contact copper, cord-impressed pottery, and early forest-steppe horse exploitation prior to Yamnaya wheeled wagons.
evidence.limits: Famous 'cult stallion' skull with bit wear was later redated by AMS to an intrusive Scythian Iron Age pit.

evidence.title: Bouar Megalithic Tazunu Pillar Monuments (Western Central African Republic)
evidence.dateBasis: Charcoal dates beneath 110+ upright granite slabs on the Yom watershed ridge.
evidence.summary: Hundreds of grouped granite megaliths (up to 3.5 m high) erected atop watershed mounds—marking one of Central Africa's earliest megalithic funerary landscapes at the Adamawa–Ubangian savanna threshold.
evidence.limits: Soil acidity prevents bone recovery inside chamber cists, leaving builders' linguistic identity debated.

evidence.title: Obobogo & Nkometou Yaoundé Early Iron & Pit Villages (South Cameroon)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon on deep bell-shaped refuse pits containing oil-palm nuts, Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum at Abang Minko), and early iron slag.
evidence.summary: Benchmark rainforest fringe agrarian villages on the Yaoundé plateau proving early Pearl millet & banana adaptation alongside rapid local iron-smelting onset prior to deep Congo Basin dispersal.
evidence.limits: Urban expansion of Yaoundé covers surrounding unexcavated pit villages.

evidence.title: Uushgiin Uvur Deer Stones & Khirigsuur Ritual Complex (Mongolia)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS dating on hundreds of surrounding sacrificed horse-head mounds bracketing 30+ carved leaping-stag stelae.
evidence.summary: Monumental Bronze Age Mongolian sanctuary featuring granite deer stones draped in stylized reindeer, warriors' belts, daggers, and bow-cases beside giant khirigsuur stone circles.
evidence.limits: Carved monoliths themselves are stylistic while sacrificial equine mounds provide firm AMS chronologies.

evidence.title: Ordu-Baliq (Khar Balgas) Uyghur Khaganate Imperial Capital (Orkhon Valley)
evidence.dateBasis: Trilingual (Uyghur, Sogdian, Chinese) Karabalghasun inscription, 32 km urban grid, and Tang/Manichaean palace bricks.
evidence.summary: Massive 32-square-kilometer cosmopolitan Silk Road metropolis along the Orkhon River founded by the Uyghur Khaganate (~751 CE), uniting nomadic military aristocracy, Manichaean Sogdian scriptoria, and irrigated farms prior to the 840 CE Yenisei Kirghiz sack.
evidence.limits: Burned in 840 CE, remaining largely unexcavated outside its citadel and Manichaean stupa core.
